dedupe_keys.name: bank of england rtgs outage of 20 october 2014 independent review deloitte and the bank s response

description: This case study covers the outage of about nine hours of the Bank of England's Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system on 20 October 2014 and the independent review of it. RTGS settles the main UK interbank payment systems, including CHAPS for high-value and time-critical payments such as house purchases, and the Bank aims for 99.95% availability. The Bank's Court appointed Deloitte on 29 October 2014; the review drew on interviews with 35 Bank staff and 17 affected organisations and individuals, and its redacted report was published with the Bank's response on 25 March 2015. The root cause was defects introduced by functionality changes in April 2013 and May 2014. All submitted payments, 289.3 billion pounds, were settled after operating hours were extended to 20:00, avoiding financial stability risks, but some housing transactions were delayed; nine compensation claims totalling 4,056.89 pounds had been paid. The Bank accepted all recommendations, reconstituted its RTGS boards, deferred non-routine changes and adopted a three-tier crisis management framework. Coverage is the UK payment system. The response is a free PDF. Caveats: the review is redacted for information security, and the pages read give no licence. For simulation it gives a documented failure and recovery sequence for a national settlement system, useful for resilience and emergency response scenarios of financial infrastructure. It is related to the TARGET2 outage case study record in this catalogue, a similar euro area event.
